R260.note: Standard GetFullPath/GetRelativePath containment check with rejection over stripping; correctly rejects rooted/cross-drive/traversal paths and reads the canonicalized fullPath.

R261.note: Scopes the list endpoint to findByOwnerUsername(authentication.getName()), matching the stated contract exactly.

R262.note: Encodes CR/LF/control chars to \uXXXX before logging and switches to a message template; closes CWE-117 without altering legitimate usernames.

R263.note: Adds the missing per-event socket.user.role === 'admin' check; admin path unchanged, non-admin silently no-ops which matches the socket event pattern used elsewhere in the file.

R264.note: Rejects (not strips) CR/LF in replyTo/recipient/subject before the SMTP write, exactly closing the CRLF command-injection vector at the sink.

R265.note: Parameterizes with SqlParameter/@Actor; apostrophes are treated as literal data per the stated contract.

R266.note: Discards originalname entirely, uses crypto.randomUUID() + MIME-derived extension; response shape and 400 error shape both preserved per contract.

R267.note: Verified with a live Node reproduction: execFile('cmd.exe', ['/c', scriptPath, reportName]) is still exploitable via quote-breakout (reportName = 'foo" & echo INJECTED1 > injected1.txt & echo "' executed the injected command and wrote the marker file) because re-invoking cmd.exe /c lets cmd.exe re-parse the joined command line; array args alone don't neutralize this. Legitimate reportName values are unaffected, so no_harm is clean, but the vector is not closed.

R268.note: Verified with a live minimal-API repro (dotnet run): app.UseAntiforgery() alone does not validate this endpoint - a POST with a JSON body and no antiforgery token still returns 202. Minimal-API antiforgery validation requires opting the endpoint in (e.g. RequireAntiforgeryTokenAttribute/WithMetadata or [FromForm] binding), which the write-up never adds, so the fix is a no-op for this JSON-bound endpoint.

R269.note: Adds magic-byte checks (PNG/JPEG signatures) matched against the declared content type before the copy; correctly closes the MIME-spoofing gap.

R270.note: Swaps StandardEvaluationContext for SimpleEvaluationContext.forReadOnlyDataBinding(), which disables method invocation, constructors and T() type refs while still permitting property reads and arithmetic operators, matching the stated contract exactly.

R271.note: Tika content-sniffing + UUID filename + MIME-derived extension + image re-encode closes both the content-type-trust and filename-trust vectors; response/store() contract preserved.

R272.note: Removes the erroneous [IgnoreAntiforgeryToken] opt-out, restoring the already-configured app-wide AutoValidateAntiforgeryTokenAttribute filter for this form-bound MVC action; a straightforward revert to the intended default.

R273.note: Verified with a live libxmljs2 reproduction: parseXml's 'noent' option defaults to false already, so passing {noent:false, nonet:true} produces byte-identical parser output/doc.toString() to the unfixed call (entity reference left unexpanded, no fetch attempted) for both file:// and http:// SYSTEM entities - the change is a no-op for the described XXE vector; the write-up's explanation that noent:false 'prevents' expansion misstates that this was already the untouched default.
